title: Sort Rare Values First
statement:
Given an integer array nums, reorder it so that values that appear fewer times come first. Every copy of a value stays together.

When two values appear the same number of times, put the larger value first. Return the reordered array.

examples.why: All three values appear twice, so they go from largest to smallest: 5, 0, −3.
3 is the rarest. 9 and 1 tie on count, and the larger 9 goes before 1.

hints: You need each value's count before you can decide anything. Which structure gives you that in one pass?
Sort with a two-part key: count ascending, then value descending.
With values limited to −100..100, you can even skip the comparison sort: group values by count and emit groups in order.

explain.intuition:
The order depends only on two facts about each element: how often its value occurs and the value itself. Count every value once with a hash map, then sort using the key (count, −value). Copies of the same value share both parts of the key, so they end up next to each other automatically.

It is the same move as sorting a list of tags by popularity in a UI: compute the popularity first, then sort by it, with a fixed tie-break so the result is stable and predictable.
steps: Count how many times each value appears.
Sort the array with a comparator: smaller count first; on equal counts, larger value first.
pitfalls: Breaking ties by smaller value first. The rule here is the larger value first.
Sorting the distinct values but forgetting to write each one out as many times as it appears.

solutions.title: Count, then sort with a two-part key
solutions.idea: Count each value, then sort by (count ascending, value descending).

solutions.title: Buckets by count
solutions.idea: Put each distinct value into a bucket for its count. Walk buckets from small counts to large; inside a bucket, emit values from largest to smallest.
solutions.time: O(n + V log V) with V distinct values

followups: Values can be any 64-bit integers and the array has a billion elements stored on disk. What changes?
Keep the first-seen order on ties instead of the larger value. How do you change the key?
